stage6.name: Stage 6: Year-Weighted Constructor
stage6.description: Dirichlet-Multinomial with recency-weighted constructor priors. Best calibrated model (LL/race = -59.0). Trained 2015-2025.

stage9.name: Stage 9: Bayesian State-Space
stage9.description: Random walk on driver/constructor log-strengths with Plackett-Luce observations. Best top-3 accuracy (1.59/3). Trained 2015-2025.

composite.name: Composite (2-Model Blend)
composite.description: Equal-weight blend of Stage 6 + Stage 9 probabilities, renormalized.

agent_prediction.name: Agent Forecast (Claude)
agent_prediction.description: Predicted by Claude using web-searched current form, prior-season results, and qualitative judgment.
agent_prediction.rationale:
The composite model has Norris (31.8%) and Antonelli (32.3%) effectively tied for the win and rates Russell P5 at 16% behind Verstappen and Piastri. I lean a little harder on the Mercedes side and push Russell up to the podium for two track-specific reasons the quantitative models can't see directly:

1. **Antonelli has momentum and circuit-specific positive priors.** He has won three in a row (China, Japan, Miami) and took his maiden F1 podium at this exact track in 2025 â€” a result the rookie-year model doesn't fully capture given his short history.
2. **Russell is the strongest Canada specialist on the grid.** He won 2025 Montreal from pole (Mercedes' first Canada win since 2019) and was P3 in 2024. The Stage 6 + Stage 9 blend doesn't include circuit-specific priors (Stage 5 was archived for destructive interaction with constructor recency), so it under-rates Russell's particular fit here.
3. **Verstappen's track history is real but Red Bull's 2026 reliability is fragile.** He's won 3 of the last 4 Montreal races (2022/23/24), but Hadjar DNF'd Miami, Verstappen took a pit-exit penalty, and Red Bull sit fourth in constructors with 29 points. I keep him in the top 5 but out of my podium.
4. **McLaren's Miami upgrade was confirmed real.** Norris took sprint pole and finished P2 in the GP; Piastri P3. They are clearly the second-fastest car. Norris is my safest pick for a podium â€” but I expect the lead Mercedes to win at a track where Mercedes have historically had sharp pace.

My podium: Antonelli, Norris, Russell. The biggest disagreement with the composite is swapping Verstappen out for Russell at P3.
context: Standings after R4 Miami: Antonelli 100, Russell 80, Leclerc 63, Norris 51, Hamilton 49 (drivers); Mercedes 181, Ferrari 112, McLaren 94, Red Bull 29 (constructors)
Antonelli has won 3 GPs in a row (R2 China, R3 Japan, R4 Miami) and currently leads the championship
2025 Canadian GP: Russell won from pole, Verstappen P2, Antonelli P3 (maiden podium)
2024 Canadian GP: Verstappen won (rain), Norris P2, Russell P3
McLaren introduced a 'completely new' car at Miami; Norris took sprint pole and finished P2 in the main race
Red Bull reliability concerns: Hadjar DNF'd Miami (lap 4 accident), Verstappen took a pit-exit penalty in Miami
Ferrari hit with multiple penalties at Miami; Leclerc P8 finish despite starting P3
